findings.trigger: A strategy card changes after load_all parses defaults but before StrategySet rereads bytes for its public version/card hash. The returned fast=20 parameters are falsely bound to the fast=21 source bytes.
findings.fix: Read each card once through load_all(read_text=...) and retain that same byte snapshot for both hashes; stable-card version algorithm is preserved.

findings.trigger: --secret-file points at a POSIX FIFO with no writer. Blocking os.open happens before fstat can reject a nonregular file, so even a disarmed webhook command hangs forever.
findings.fix: Add O_NONBLOCK to the existing O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW open; retain regular-file, owner and private-mode checks before reading or starting a listener.

findings.trigger: Opening an owned legacy archive with an incompatible writer first constructs Store, which creates graph tables and updates user_version before OracleEngine notices the incompatible evaluator policy. Refusal still changes the supposedly preserved archive bytes.
findings.fix: Engine passes the canonical expected policy into Store; Store validates recorded identity inside its initialization transaction before any DDL, persistent PRAGMA or chmod. Existing later policy check remains.

findings.trigger: If an archive retains observations but its metadata policy row is missing, a new engine with a different horizon inserts its own policy over that history. Prior observations acquire a new identity without generating new evidence.
findings.fix: Before initializing/migrating, reject an absent policy whenever any known evidence table is nonempty; a truly empty archive remains initializable. No old-hash allowlist or evidence relabeling.

findings.trigger: The legacy graph test uses sqlite3.Connection as a transaction context and never closes the connection; Python3.13 emits ResourceWarning: unclosed database after fixture collection.
findings.fix: Wrap both legacy fixture transactions in contextlib.closing and preserve the transaction context; no assertions removed.
findings.test: ResourceWarning capture around GraphDBTests.test_legacy_archive_reports_missing_graph_without_writing followed by gc.collect()

findings.trigger: Missing numpy in a normal Oracle command or missing mcp at server import emits an uncaught traceback/exit1. MCP --help also fails before argument parsing when the protocol SDK is absent.
findings.fix: Delay optional protocol imports to the first SDK use, parse help first, and return exit3 with fixed prerequisite code plus an isolated uv repair command for known missing package names. Library SDK operations retain normal missing-dependency errors.

findings.trigger: Invalid CLI input prints only a fixed error sentence. It omits usage, leaving no discoverable correction; the server likewise emits only a generic unavailable sentence.
findings.fix: Print parser usage before fixed sanitized errors; exit2 stays unchanged and untrusted argument values are never included.

findings.trigger: Setup documents old absolute source paths and a multi-package ad-hoc environment while later prose claims evaluator identities stay unchanged. Current source changes necessarily create a new identity and must not be confused with frozen installed copies.
findings.fix: Use the existing repository-root uv/.venv setup and one installed CLI invocation, explain prerequisite/usage behavior, optional manager integration and original pinned archive identities/new archive writer fences.
findings.test: README commands compared with actual console entrypoints/manifests; --help, preflight, usage and identity-fence tests pass.
